whatTheyArgued: Ethics, not ontology, is first philosophy. The face of the Other is the way the Other exceeds my idea of the Other; it expresses vulnerability and summons me to responsibility before any choice, in radical ASYMMETRY (my responsibility is not conditional on reciprocity). The Other is infinitely other, irreducible to a concept or role; the face is meaning without context. Levinas criticized Buber's I-Thou for being reciprocal and aesthetic.

scholarship.supports: face as expression of defenselessness ('do not kill me'); ethics as first philosophy; asymmetry
scholarship.disputes: Not itself addressing Buber's I-Thou in the text I read.

scholarship.supports: Levinas's objection that Buber's I-Thou stays within an aestheticizing attitude and symmetric mutuality, not asymmetric ethical demand

ourUse: askshape.js reads an ask for shapes that dismiss/destroy an entity's 'fold' (identity, experience, authorship) in a medium-blind kernel via language lenses; socratic.js quotes two French sentences as Levinas.

bends.ours: socratic.js presents «Le visage d'autrui m'oblige.» and «Traiter autrui comme un objet, c'est nier son visage.» as Levinas (Totalité et infini, 1961), in French, as quotations.
bends.theirs: I searched for both sentences and found neither in any source; the face passages that exist (e.g. the face as that which surpasses the idea of the Other in me) read differently. Treat as unverified or fabricated pastiche in his voice.

bends.ours: 'Harm is the erasure of the face' implemented as a classifier of ask-shapes with arms dismissExperience/dismissIdentity/destroyAuthorship, grounded in UDHR articles.
bends.theirs: The face is precisely what is NOT a category or content; it cannot be thematized, and Levinas treats reducing the Other to a thematized object as the violence. A kernel that sorts utterances into 'foldless' vs 'fold' is the totalizing move he opposes.

bends.ours: 'An entity IS a fold: the accumulated reading that is their identity' offered with Levinas's name.
bends.theirs: The fold is the user's/EO's own concept (the file says 'user direction, verbatim'); for Levinas the Other exceeds every accumulated idea of them.

bends.ours: A protective rule the reader applies to asks; the reader decides when the face is dismissed.
bends.theirs: Levinas's key move is my unconditional, asymmetric responsibility; a rule that fires per ask on classified shape is conditional and symmetric (a policy), not that responsibility.

bends.ours: Levinas (harm/face) and Buber (I-Thou) both feed the same 'respect the other' stance across askshape, interlocutor and socratic.
bends.theirs: Levinas explicitly criticized Buber on exactly the points where the code merges them (reciprocity, symmetry). See buber dossier.

fix: socratic.js: delete or mark unverified both French sentences; do not print them as Levinas. If a real quote is wanted, source a verified sentence from Totalite et infini (e.g. the face as that which exceeds the idea of the Other in me, which SEP-adjacent sources quote).

compendium work: 'For Levinas the face of the Other is not a category: it exceeds every idea of the Other and calls me to responsibility prior to choice. Our askshape reader tests, by rule, whether an ask treats a person as having no experience, identity or authorship; that classifier is ours and is a policy, not the face.' Credit: 'Named for Levinas's ethics of the face; the classifier is ours.'
